content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed an operational handbook on tuberculosis (TB) prevention, specifically focusing on TB preventive treatment. This handbook, titled Module 1: Prevention Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment, is available in both electronic and print versions, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-000290-6 and 978-92-4-000291-3. Published in 2020, the handbook is distributed under a Creative Commons license, allowing users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the content for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. If a translation is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not produced by WHO and that the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The handbook emphasizes that WHO does not endorse any specific organizations, products, or services mentioned within the publication. Any disputes arising under the license are to be mediated according to the rules of the World Intellectual Property Organization. The suggested citation for the handbook is: WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis. Module 1: prevention tuberculosis preventive treatment. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2020. The handbook includes detailed chapters covering various aspects of TB prevention and treatment, such as identifying populations for TB preventive treatment, ruling out active TB disease before initiating preventive treatment, testing for TB infection, administering TB preventive treatment, managing safety and adverse drug reactions, ensuring adherence to treatment, monitoring and evaluation, and addressing ethical considerations. Additionally, annexes provide key messages, coordination mechanisms, cost considerations, planning checklists, and answers to frequently asked questions about tuberculin skin tests (TST) and interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs). The handbook was prepared by Avinash Kanchar with contributions from Dennis Falzon and Matteo Zignol, under the direction of Tereza Kasaeva, Director of the WHO Global TB Programme. The WHO acknowledges the contributions of numerous experts, reviewers, and organizations involved in the development of the 2020 guidelines on TB preventive treatment, which form the basis of this handbook. The Guideline Development Group (GDG) included experts from various countries and institutions, with co-chairs Lindiwe Mvusi and Nandi Siegfried, the latter also serving as the GRADE methodologist. Observers from organizations such as USAID, UNITAID, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and the Stop TB Partnership also participated in the guideline revision process. An External Review Group (ERG) provided additional input, and public feedback was solicited during the draft review phase in early 2020. Evidence reviewers from institutions like McGill University, Johns Hopkins University, and the University of Nebraska contributed to the evidence summaries for the guidelines. The handbook defines key terms used throughout the document, such as active case finding (systematic screening for TB disease), latent TB infection (a state of immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens without clinical disease), and TB preventive treatment (interventions to reduce the risk of developing TB disease in at-risk individuals). It also outlines the responsibilities of healthcare providers and communities in scaling up TB preventive treatment through programmatic management. The WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in this publication, but it is distributed without warranty. The responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader, and WHO is not liable for any damages arising from its use. The design and layout of the handbook were funded by Unitaid, and acknowledgments are extended to all contributors and reviewers involved in its production.
